scope: Complete execution of all 22 triggered effect shapes and ordered riders over live game state.

fullGameReplayMemory.scope: Fresh processes on the same C driver. Peak requested bytes include parsing the full test bundle, initialization, gameplay, observer serialization and disposal. Allocation request counts include reallocations. Live gameplay memory and whole-process RSS require separate measurements.

performance.scope: Fixed summon-cap queries on sparse and crowded synthetic rosters. Embedded allocations cover the whole VM lifecycle. Target-device and game-frame measurements remain open.

discoveries: Cue ordering and hard-control cleansing initially escaped weak independent assertions. The corrected cases detect both faults.
A focused installed cleanse control had listed the status explicitly. An authored record that selects by status class detects the injected fault.
The initial public declarations collapsed two discriminators and restricted summon ownership to actor objects. Typed consumers now select either hit variant and accept numeric owner zero.
The adapter installer retains another writer’s truncated or replaced binding after a failed World replacement. It removes only the bytes it wrote on its own failed installation.
limitations: The game continues to own geometry, physics, real hit delivery and actor construction. The extracted dispatcher orchestrates those services.
Replay through C/C++/.NET is an embedded development proof. A drop-in bridge for this capability in other engines is still open.
The trusted effect grammar does not validate third-party packs. Physical Steam Deck/mobile and whole-game frame performance remain unmeasured.

raw.contents: Verification receipts, per-command logs, focused fault observations, native metrics and benchmark distributions. Large repeated native outputs are represented by verified content hashes.
